q1_issues.issue: The query hard-codes the invented witness symbol sk_generation_1 instead of binding the definite 'the present generation' as a variable constrained by its kind, so it can only match a KB that happens to have minted that exact symbol.
(GroupOf sk_generation_1 keeper) builds into the pattern that the generation is a group whose members are keepers, which the question does not state - it says Keepers are active in that generation.
The partitive superset/SubsetOf machinery is used although the question carries no 'of the / of them' partitive cue, so the pattern matches only a partitive storage the sentence never licenses.

(Inheritance $g active) predicates the property of a group witness with Inheritance, which is licensed only for a partitive subset group; a copular predicate over a plural is stored as a per-member distribution rule, not as an atom on the group.

q2_gaps: a counting question whose predicate is copular ('how many Ns are ADJ?') - the Counting-questions shape anchors the counted group to an event, and a copular predicate over a plural is stored as a per-member distribution rule that a flat query conjunct cannot bind
notes: Only (GroupOf $g keeper) (Cardinality $g $n) is well-formed; everything anchoring the count to the question's restriction is invented structure. 'In the present generation' is never given the reified-state plus preposition-named In oblique route the instruction set would allow.
